# @loushy/build-ai-agent

> A TypeScript SDK for building AI agents that run in your own code, on your own host: a typed tool-calling loop with approvals, sessions, streaming, sub-agents, skills, MCP and a CLI, with no web framework or hosted runtime required. It is for developers who need an agent to keep working when a run pauses for a human or the process restarts, and who want to test it like the rest of their code.

## Docs

- [@loushy/build-ai-agent](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/README.md): A TypeScript SDK for building AI agents that run in your own code, on your own host: a typed tool-calling loop with approvals, sessions, streaming, sub-agents, skills, MCP and a CLI, with no web framework or hosted runtime required.
- [Installation](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/installation.md): `ai` (the Vercel AI SDK, `^4.3.19`) and `zod` (`^3.25.76`) are required peer dependencies.
- [Quick Start](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/quick-start.md): Every TypeScript snippet on this page is a complete, standalone ES module (`.mts`).
- [API Overview](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/api-overview.md): The package root (`@loushy/build-ai-agent`) exports everything below.
- [Agent Client Protocol (ACP)](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/acp.md): The Agent Client Protocol lets an editor drive a coding agent that runs as a subprocess: the editor writes JSON-RPC 2.0 requests to the agent's stdin, one JSON message per line, and reads the agent's replies and streamed updates from its stdout.
- [Agent directories](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/agent-directories.md): An agent can be defined as a directory.
- [AI SDK UI (`useChat`)](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/ai-sdk-ui.md): If your front end already uses the Vercel AI SDK's UI hooks (`useChat` from `@ai-sdk/react`, and the Vue, Svelte and Angular equivalents), you can keep them and run a Loushy agent behind the route.
- [Approvals](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/approvals.md): Flag a tool `needsApproval` and the run pauses before calling it, until a human (or your code) approves or rejects the call.
- [Channels](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/channels.md): A channel connects an agent to one surface: a JSON API, a webhook, a chat app.
- [CLI](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/cli.md): Installing the package also installs the `loushy` command.
- [Context compaction](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/compaction.md): A long agent run fills its context window mostly with tool results: file contents, search hits, API responses the model read once and no longer needs in full.
- [Configuration](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/configuration.md): A declarative agent is a YAML (`.yaml`/`.yml`) or JSON (`.json`) file, validated with zod by `loadSpec()` (`src/spec/schema.ts`).
- [Durable execution](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/durable-execution.md): Pass a `sessionId` and a `checkpointStore` to `AgentExecutor.execute()` and the run survives a crash, a restart, an abort or a human approval that takes days.
- [Errors](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/errors.md): Every error the SDK throws on purpose is an `SDKError` (or a subclass such as `ConfigurationError`, `ValidationError` or `MissingPeerDependencyError`) with
- [Evals](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/evals.md): Evals are regression tests for agent *behaviour*: which tools the agent called, in what order, with which arguments, how many steps it took, and what it said.
- [Flows](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/flows.md): A flow is a fixed, multi-step workflow run by one agent: the steps and their order are written down up front instead of being left to the model's judgment.
- [Guardrails and sandboxing](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/guardrails.md): Tools for running agents safely: input and output guardrails check what goes into and comes out of any run (and its tool arguments), patch guardrails are fail-closed checks over a proposed change before you act on it, and sandboxed tools run inside an isolated container instead of the host process.
- [Memory](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/memory.md): A session remembers one conversation.
- [Tracing and observability](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/observability.md): `AgentExecutor.execute()` and `FlowExecutor.execute()` emit spans through a `TraceExporter`.
- [Providers](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/providers.md): An `LLMProvider` is what an agent generates with.
- [React](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/react.md): `useLoushyAgent()` puts an agent behind a chat UI.
- [Schedules](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/schedules.md): A schedule runs the agent on a cron expression, with nobody asking: a morning summary, a nightly cleanup.
- [Sessions](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/sessions.md): `agent.send(text)` is single-turn: every call starts from an empty history.
- [Skills](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/skills.md): A skill is a named chunk of instructions (a markdown document) that the model loads only when it needs it.
- [Streaming](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/streaming.md): `agent.stream()` runs an agent exactly like `agent.send()` and reports the run as a stream of typed events: model text as it arrives, every tool call, step boundaries, approval requests, and a final `run.done`.
- [Structured output](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/structured-output.md): Give an agent a zod schema as `output` and its final reply becomes a typed, validated object: `result.object`.
- [Sub-agents](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/sub-agents.md): A sub-agent is a separate agent - its own instructions, model, tools and skills - that a lead agent hands a self-contained task to.
- [Svelte](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/svelte.md): `loushyAgent()` for Svelte is the React hook as a store: the same sources, the same state and the same actions, over the same typed event stream.
- [Testing agents](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/testing.md): `@loushy/build-ai-agent/testing` ships `mockModel`: a scripted, deterministic `LLMProvider` for unit tests.
- [Tools](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/tools.md): A tool is a typed function the model can call.
- [Utilities](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/utilities.md): Supporting helpers exported from the package root: encryption and hashing, file storage for attachments, and template rendering.
- [Vue](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/vue.md): `useLoushyAgent()` for Vue 3 is the React hook as a composable: the same sources, the same state and the same actions, over the same typed event stream.
- [Workspace tools](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/workspace-tools.md): Workspace tools give an agent a file system and a shell, so you can build coding agents in the style of Claude Code.

## Examples

- [agent-dir](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/examples/agent-dir/README.md): An agent defined as a directory: `instructions.md` is the system prompt, `tools/word_count.ts` is a `defineTool()` tool, `skills/tone.md` is a skill and `agent.json` holds config.
- [doc-qa](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/examples/doc-qa/README.md): A question-answering agent scoped to a single fixed document (a short refund policy, inlined in the prompt), built with `createAgent()`.
- [openrouter](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/examples/openrouter/README.md): Runnable snippets showing `OpenRouterProvider` usage (LOU-B6): basic and streaming generation, multi-model comparison, tool calling, `AgentBuilder` configuration, model listing, cost-aware model choice, error handling, multi-turn conversation, and capability checks.
- [ops-pipeline (LOU-J8)](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/examples/ops-pipeline/README.md): An end-to-end "flagship pipeline" demo composing every LOU-J primitive
- [research-assistant](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/examples/research-assistant/README.md): An agent with the built-in `http` tool wired up so it can fetch sources while researching a question, built with `createAgent()`.
- [slack-notifier](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/examples/slack-notifier/README.md): Turns a raw event description into a short, Slack-ready notification message, built with `createAgent()`.
- [support-bot](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/examples/support-bot/README.md): A minimal customer-support agent built with `createAgent()`.
- [workflow-router](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/examples/workflow-router/README.md): An agent that classifies an incoming request into one of a fixed set of categories (`billing`/`technical`/`sales`), built with `createAgent()`.

## Optional

- [Agent Forge](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/agent-forge.md): Agent Forge (`apps/agent-forge`) is this SDK's companion visual dashboard: build an agent's graph on a canvas, run it, watch it execute in a live debug console, chat with it, and author sandboxed pre/post hooks - all reading and writing the exact same `AgentSpec` YAML that `loushy dev` and `loushy build` use.
- [Deployment](https://github.com/LinuxDevil/agent-sdk/blob/main/docs/deployment.md): `loushy build` turns an agent spec file (see Configuration) into a deployable artifact for one target platform
